The rule has found its chief proving ground in suits on construction 
contracts. Why should this be so? Several considerations 
sugge t th,

been regarded as

employment contracts, it is usual for an employer to pay wage at short

for the sale of goods, the seller who is denied a remedy can u ually 
dispose of the goods elsewhere and will not suffer a loss comparable to 
that of the builder who cannot enforce the contract. As for land sal ,

contract ordinarily has access to the remedy of specific performanc , .
